entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Perdiccas III of Macedon was a Macedonian king from 365 BC to 360 BC, succeeding his brother Alexander II.

He played a crucial role in the Hellenistic period, particularly during the Wars of the Diadochi, as he struggled to assert his authority against rival successors.

Perdiccas' reign had significant regional implications, as it influenced the politics and geography of Macedonia and its neighboring territories.

This era marked the beginning of a new chapter in Macedonian history, one that would shape the course of the ancient world for centuries to come.
